item.title: KeyReel
item.description:
Role: co-founder and CTO of Auxoft LLC, 2015-2020.

KeyReel started as an idea. The condition for funding was a proof of concept in 2 months: a minimal Bluetooth protocol, an iPhone app, a Mac app relaying between phone and browser, and a Chrome extension that logged in to Facebook and GitHub. I built it, and the MVP got funded.

  • MVP in 4 months: a credential database on the iPhone, a macOS tray app, Chrome and Safari extensions, and a stable Bluetooth link that reconnects when the phone comes back and holds for days.
  • A product on five platforms: iOS, macOS, Windows, browser extensions and Android. I wrote 96% of the 68.5k-line Apple apps and 5,798 of the company's 8,917 commits.
  • Probabilistic login-form recognition: in an internal benchmark KeyReel auto-filled 488 of 500 sites (indicative: tuned on the same list).
  • 2FA and U2F: an authenticator inside the password database, and the phone acting as a security key through a macOS driver.
  • One extension codebase that carried KeyReel to Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge, Opera, Brave and Vivaldi.
  • In the stores: iOS app on the App Store since March 2017, rated 4.8 from 12 ratings; Android on Google Play from July 2020. Reviewed by The Mac Observer (2018), launched on ProductHunt.
  • Co-inventor of US patent 10,764,056 "Short-distance network electronic authentication" (2020).

Auxoft has since closed.
